title: Daemon visibility: ork daemon status, a daemon line in doctor, and a stale rule that ignores commits with no code change
lead: `ork daemon status` says whether the daemon runs, its pid and build, whether it is stale and whether roles run. `ork doctor` always prints a daemon line. The stale-daemon warning no longer fires for a commit that changes no file the binary is built from. This is an N-class slice (`internal/cli` only); the TUI marker keeps the old rule until the owner decides (Q-D4).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Source: the wave 4 friction log (`.scratch/v11/wave4-friction.md`, F2, F3, F26, 2026-11-02). The owner decided on 2026-11-02 (interactive question) that these status and CLI clarity slices go in pass v1.2. The stale rule is an open owner question (Q-D1); this spec pins the recommended option. Each claim was re-read at HEAD `9202ba8`.

Verified, and what this slice does about it:

- F2 (`ork daemon status` does not exist; the error reads like a state message). True. `daemonCommand` accepts only `stop` and `restart` and otherwise returns usage `daemon needs stop or restart [--force]` (`internal/cli/lifecycle.go:67-71`). `ork daemon status` printed `ork: daemon needs stop or restart [--force]` with exit 2 (run on 2026-11-02). The usage text lists `daemon run`, `stop` and `restart` (`internal/cli/cli.go:121-124`); `daemon run` is handled before the CLI is reached (`cmd/ork/main.go:86-88`), so the CLI never sees it. Fix: add `status` (a read; it must not start a daemon, as `stop` and `doctor` do not), and say `unknown daemon command "X"; use ...` for the rest.
- F3 (`ork doctor` printed no daemon line). True when the daemon is current. Doctor prints a daemon line only as a warning: `[WARN] daemon  stale daemon build ...` when the build differs and `[WARN] daemon behind main: ...` when the self-hosted daemon is behind main and idle (`internal/cli/doctor.go:453-458`). A running, current daemon and a missing daemon print nothing. The JSON has `daemon_build_id` (omitted when no daemon answers) but no running flag (`doctor.go:78-90`). The behind notice is limited to the idle point (`internal/daemon/build.go:114-125`, `BehindWarning` returns "" while roles run), so while a wave runs, which is when the owner looks, doctor says nothing about it.
- F26, part 1 (a filing-only commit marks the daemon stale). True. The build id is `vcs.revision` plus `+modified=BOOL` (adj 102, `daemon.build-id`, decided 2026-10-20; `cmd/ork/main.go:33-55`), and `StaleBuild` is a string compare (`internal/daemon/build.go:127-134`). Every commit changes the revision, including the tracking commits that change only `.slicer/` (this repository's `6d94f7e` changed only `.slicer/` files). Checked with git on 2026-11-02: `git diff --quiet b0b1130 6d94f7e` with the exclusions below exits 0 (nothing the binary is built from changed), and `b0b1130` against `2eb7fc2` exits 1 (`internal/registry/registry.go` and `internal/tui/model.go` changed). The warning on 2026-11-02 for the pair `b0b1130` and `2eb7fc2` is therefore correct; the one after the `6d94f7e` rebuild was not. `docs/design.md:74-75` already notes that revision plus modified state cannot tell two builds of different edits at one revision apart; this slice goes the other way.
- F26, part 2 (the warning repeats on every command, including `--json` on stderr). True, by design. Every daemon command passes through `withDaemon`, which calls `CheckDaemonBuild` and prints the warning to stderr (`internal/cli/cli.go:314-324`, `internal/cli/lifecycle.go:32-62`); `ork status` adds the behind notice (`internal/cli/run.go:23-33`). Tests pin the warning in `--json` mode (`internal/cli/lifecycle_test.go:280-297`). One warning per command is intended (`docs/design.md:69-71`, adj 130). With a rule that does not fire for a tracking commit, the repeat is no longer a false alarm. Whether to warn less often is Q-D2; the spec changes nothing there.
- F26, part 3 (restart is refused while roles run). True and documented (`docs/design.md:41-48`, `docs/guide.md:49`). `ork daemon status` states it.

Embedded files matter for the rule. `internal/roles/roles.go:30` embeds `prompts/*.md` into the binary, so a prompt change is a code change even though it is a `.md` file, and S233 would add another embedded `.md` (`internal/cli/ai_instructions.md`). So the rule excludes what the binary is certainly not built from, and counts everything else: `.slicer/`, `docs/`, markdown files in the repository root, `*_test.go`, `testdata/` and `.github/`.

Not in this slice: the TUI's stale marker (`internal/tui/view.go:575-579` compares build strings with `daemon.StaleBuild`; S103 reworks where the TUI gets the daemon build, and it is E-class), the `behind main` computation (S131 changes it to the base branch), F1, `ork daemon restart` itself, an auto-restart (`NEW-daemon-restart-helper`), and a wire field for roles running in `daemon.info`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Pinned options: Q-D1 b (stale only when files the binary is built from differ), Q-D2 a (warnings unchanged), Q-D3 a (doctor and `daemon status` show behind-main even while roles run), Q-D5 a (exit 0 when not running). A fake daemon is a small `ipc.Server` on a temp socket like `predatingDaemon` (`internal/cli/lifecycle_test.go:357-373`) with handlers for `daemon.info` and `status`.

Part A, `ork daemon status`:

- `TestDaemonStatusReportsARunningDaemon` (`internal/cli/daemonstatus_test.go`): text has `daemon: running`, `pid: N` (from `App.Pid`), `socket: PATH`, `build: REV12` and `state: current`; `--json` is `{"running":true,"pid":N,"socket":...,"build_id":...,"cli_build_id":...,"stale":false,"roles_running":false,"behind_main":false}`. Fails first: `daemon needs stop or restart` and exit 2.
- `TestDaemonStatusDoesNotStartADaemon`: no socket, `App.Start` fails the test if called; text `daemon: not running`, JSON `{"running":false,"socket":...,"cli_build_id":...}`; exit 0. Fails first: usage error.
- `TestDaemonStatusSaysStale`: the daemon reports another non-hex build: `state: stale (the CLI build differs; run ork daemon restart)`, `"stale":true`, and no warning on stderr (the command is not run through `withDaemon`). Fails first: usage error.
- `TestDaemonStatusSaysRolesRunAndRestartIsRefused`: `status` reports `roles_running: true`: text `roles: running (ork daemon restart is refused; --force cancels them)`. Fails first: usage error.
- `TestDaemonStatusSaysBehindMainEvenWhileRolesRun`: a self-hosted project with `behind_main` true and roles running: `main: behind (restart waits for the roles, or use --force)`, `"behind_main":true`. Fails first: usage error.
- `TestDaemonStatusSurvivesAFailedStatusRead`: `daemon.info` answers and `status` fails: build and pid still print, the roles and main lines are left out, exit 0. Fails first: usage error.
- `TestDaemonUnknownSubcommandSaysSo`: `daemon bogus` exits 2 with `ork: unknown daemon command "bogus"; use status, stop, restart or run`; `daemon` alone exits 2 with `ork: daemon needs status, stop, restart or run`; `daemon status extra` exits 2 with `daemon status takes no arguments`. Fails first: the old text.
- `TestUsageListsDaemonStatus`: the help text has the `ork daemon status` line and every line stays within 80 columns. Fails first: no line.

Part A, doctor:

- `TestDoctorPrintsADaemonLineWhenCurrent`: `[ok] daemon  running, build REV12 (pid N)` and, in the JSON, `daemon_running` true and `daemon_pid` N, with no WARN line. Fails first: no line.
- `TestDoctorPrintsADaemonLineWhenNoneRuns`: `[--] daemon  not running; the next command starts it`, JSON `daemon_running` false, doctor starts no daemon and the exit code is unchanged. Fails first: no line.
- `TestDoctorBehindMainShowsWhileRolesRun`: status with `roles_running` true and `behind_main` true prints the behind line with `(roles are running; restart waits)`; `daemon.BehindWarning` itself is unchanged. Fails first: the line is missing while roles run.
- `TestDoctorStaleDaemonWarning` (existing, `lifecycle_test.go:322-355`) still passes with its non-hex builds.

Part B, the stale rule (`internal/cli/stale_test.go`), with real `git` in a temp repository for the pathspec test and `clitest` fake git routes for the rest:

- `TestStalePathspecCountsOnlyWhatTheBinaryIsBuiltFrom` (real git): commits that change only `.slicer/x.json`, `docs/a.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `a_test.go`, `testdata/x`, `.github/y` give `git diff --quiet` exit 0 with the pathspec; a commit that changes `internal/roles/prompts/a.md`, `x.go`, `go.mod` or `cmd/ork/main.go` gives exit 1. Fails first: no pathspec constant.
- `TestStaleTrackingOnlyCommitIsNotStale`: daemon `R1+modified=false`, CLI `R2+modified=false` (40-hex), a registered project, fake git: `cat-file -e` ok for both and `diff --quiet` exit 0: no warning in text or `--json` mode (stderr empty), and `daemon status` says `state: current (the CLI build differs only in files the binary is not built from)`. Fails first: the warning prints.
- `TestStaleCodeChangeIsStale`: `diff --quiet` exit 1: the existing warning text prints once. Passes before and after; it guards the rule.
- `TestStaleFailsSafe` (table): no registry file; registry without a project that has both commits (`cat-file` exit 1 for each); `diff` exit 128; either build `modified=true`; same revision with different `modified`; non-hex ids (`old`, `unknown`, ``, `dev`): each is stale. Passes before and after (today every difference is stale); it guards the fail-safe branches of the new rule against a later change.
- `TestStaleTakesTheFirstProjectWithBothCommits`: three registered projects; only the second has both commits; the diff runs with `-C` of the second; later projects get no git call.
- `TestEqualBuildsAskGitNothing`: equal ids make no git call (`fake.CallsTo("git")` is empty).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Tests first, in the order above (part A, then part B). Confirm each fails for its reason.
2. `internal/cli/stale.go`:
   - `const engineChangePathspec`: the `git diff --quiet R1 R2 -- . ':(exclude).slicer' ':(exclude)docs' ':(exclude,glob)*.md' ':(exclude,glob)**/*_test.go' ':(exclude)testdata' ':(exclude).github'` arguments, as one slice of strings. Checked with git on 2026-11-02 in this repository.
   - `func (a *App) staleBuild(ctx context.Context, daemonBuild string) (stale bool, note string)`. Equal ids: not stale. Either id not a 40- or 64-hex revision, or either `+modified=true`, or the daemon id empty or `unknown`: stale. Otherwise read the registry (`registry.DefaultPath`, `registry.Load`, as `doctor.go` does), and for each project in order run `git -C PATH cat-file -e REV^{commit}` for both revisions; for the first project that has both, run the diff with the pathspec. Exit 0: not stale, with `note` naming that the CLI build differs only in files the binary is not built from. Exit 1: stale. Any other result, or no such project: stale. Use `Tools.Git` when set, else `git`. Use a short timeout (the `versionTimeout` that doctor uses).
   - `staleWarning(ctx, build)` calls it; `warnStale`, `CheckDaemonBuild` and `callWith` pass their context.
   - Leave `daemon.StaleBuild` as it is. Do not edit `internal/daemon` or the TUI (Q-D4).
3. `internal/cli/daemonstatus.go`: `daemon status` dials without starting (as `stop` does, treat a missing socket and a refused connection as not running); asks `daemon.info` (an `unknown_method` reply means build `unknown`, as `daemonBuild` does); reads the pid from `App.Pid` (missing or unreadable: `pid: unknown`); then reads `status` once for `roles_running` and the self-host `behind_main` flag, and drops those lines when the read fails. It does not use `withDaemon` (that would print the stale warning on top of the stale line). Text and JSON as in the tests; the build text is the first 12 characters of the revision, plus `+modified` when modified. JSON fields are *proposed*.
4. `daemonCommand`: add `status`; change the usage messages to the pinned text. Keep `stop` and `restart` as they are.
5. `doctor.go`: add `DaemonRunning bool json:"daemon_running"` and `DaemonPID int json:"daemon_pid,omitempty"`; print the ok, not-running and behind lines as pinned. Keep the existing stale WARN line (full ids) when stale.
6. Docs: `docs/design.md` (the build check: the rule, the pathspec and why embedded prompts count; the usage list), `docs/guide.md`, `docs/dashboard.md`. Mark the rule and the command *proposed* until the owner records Q-D1 in adj (suggest key `daemon.stale-rule`).
7. Do NOT touch `internal/daemon`, `internal/engine`, `cmd`, `internal/tui`. Do not restart a daemon or run `ork daemon restart` from tests (use fake sockets).
8. CHANGELOG entry last, under `## Unreleased`, marked *proposed*.
9. UI slice: UI pass (r14).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- From the worktree: `git diff --quiet b0b1130 6d94f7e -- . ':(exclude).slicer' ':(exclude)docs' ':(exclude,glob)*.md' ':(exclude,glob)**/*_test.go' ':(exclude)testdata' ':(exclude).github'` exits 0 and the same command with `2eb7fc2` exits 1.
- [HUMAN CHECK] After landing and a rebuild of `~/bin/ork` and a restart, the owner runs `ork daemon status`, `ork doctor` and `ork status` once with the daemon running, and once after a commit that only touches `.slicer/` (no warning expected), and after a Go change (warning expected).
